claims.text: As-solidified FeNiCrMn has a primarily single-phase, likely FCC structure.
Dynamic deformation of as-solidified FeNiCrMn involves rapid dislocation nucleation.
Localized adiabatic heating causes adiabatic shear-band formation in FeNiCrMn.
Adiabatic shear bands act as sites for dynamic recrystallization.
Shear-band-associated dynamic recrystallization refines the FeNiCrMn microstructure.
Dynamic recrystallization within shear bands enhances local yield strength and work hardening.
Excessive localization into adiabatic shear bands promotes embrittlement and loss of ductility.
The balance between strain-rate-induced strengthening and localized-deformation embrittlement governs the strength–ductility performance of FeNiCrMn.
Higher strain rates increase the dynamic yield strength of as-solidified FeNiCrMn.
Higher strain rates produce more pronounced adiabatic shear bands.
Lower temperatures increase dynamic yield strength and promote pronounced adiabatic shear-band formation in FeNiCrMn.
Increasing adiabatic shear-band development is accompanied by greater microstructural refinement.
Greater adiabatic shear-band development correlates with reduced ductility.
Lower strain rates or moderate temperatures produce more uniform deformation, improved ductility, and less pronounced shear-band features.
Quasi-static as-solidified FeNiCrMn provides a baseline without significant shear-band formation or dynamic recrystallization.
Prior thermomechanical processing, phase changes, grain-size changes, or altered defect densities may produce deformation mechanisms different from the proposed one.
Twinning and grain-boundary-mediated deformation may contribute alongside the proposed mechanism.
The proposed study varies strain rate from approximately 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1 and temperature from 77 K to 600 K while measuring mechanical response and post-deformation microstructure.

The mechanism would be falsified by the absence of a systematic association among high strain rate, shear-band intensity, dynamic recrystallization, microstructural refinement, and mechanical-property changes, or by dominance of an alternative mechanism.
